study_metadata.title: Post-Week 4 Quantitative Feasibility, Bottleneck Root-Cause and Architecture Scaling Study

study_1_noise_vs_certified_margin_gap.scientific_conclusion: Streaming L2 displacement (mean = 24.2591) is 50990.3x larger on average than the maximum certified L2 radius (mean = 0.014479). To achieve non-zero certified reuse rate R > 0 on streaming IMU, the model's margin must be widened or Lipschitz sensitivity contracted by at least 1562.7x.

overhead_benchmarks.note_on_provenance: T_v and T_inc are proxy baseline measurements from SmallCNN1D; native Transformer attention verifier remains to be measured.

result_a_computational_crossover.summary: Theoretical computational crossover occurs at ~27.6 MMACs (~2.5M params) assuming verifier cost T_v=1.3346 ms and 100% reuse.

result_b_actual_stream_speedup.summary: On actual HAPT stream with R=0% (observed at Stride 64), ECDR incurs a 39.5% slowdown (4.72 ms vs 3.38 ms). Net speedup strictly requires certified reuse rate R > 39.5%.

study_2_break_even_model_capacity_scalin.scientific_conclusion: [Result A - Computational Crossover]: The theoretical crossover occurs at ~27.6 MMACs (~2.5M params) for verifier caching, and ~41.2 MMACs (~2.8M params) for incremental recomputation. At 5.0M parameters (TemporalTransformer1D), full inference latency is ~3.38 ms vs T_v=1.3346 ms, giving a theoretical upper-bound speedup of 2.53x. [Result B - Actual Stream Speedup]: NOT_ESTABLISHED. Because T_v was borrowed from SmallCNN1D and evaluated on random batch=1 inputs, actual streaming performance on HAPT depends on certified reuse rate R. If R=0% (as observed at Stride 64), total latency is T_v + T_full = 4.72 ms, causing a 39.5% slowdown. Net speedup strictly requires certified reuse R > 39.5%.

study_3_incremental_optimization_ceiling.scientific_conclusion: Pre-allocating in-place sliding buffers reduces intermediate conv latency from 0.034 ms to 0.033 ms (a 4.1% reduction). However, direct PyTorch C++ single-call forward (0.012 ms) remains faster than multi-stage shifting at shallow depth, confirming that fused C/CUDA kernels are mandatory for incremental net speedup on 1D CNNs.
